eu_indicator_definition: The chart provides an overview of the distribution of selected social transfers by population quintiles (fifths) from the poorest to the richest in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The study, based on APD data from 2011, estimates that the poorest fifth of the population receives only 17.3% of the total budget allocated for social protection cash benefits, meaning the impact of these benefits on reducing poverty is almost negligible. In fact, if these benefits didn’t exist at all, relative poverty in BiH would only increase by 1.7 percentage points (from 17.9% to 19.6%).
eu_rationale: The relative poverty line set at 60% of the median consumption per adult equivalent in BiH in 2011 was 416.4 KM per month for a single-member adult household in BiH.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The main objective of this research is to assess the effects of existing cash social protection programs in BiH on the incomes of poor households.
eu_long_objective: Reduce the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 15 million by 2030 compared with 2019 (polici reference: European pillar of social rights Action Plan)
indicator_name: Distribution of social protection transfers to the population in Bosnia and Herzegovina - proxy indicator
